title: [finding] ablation-replace.mjs reports a LANDED mutation as not landed whenever the replacement contains the anchor — the shape of every append-style ablation
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` 执行席 2(座位帖 #18549,会话 `session_01JbZnqu8bt6YqfJsr9vaFb3`)from the `out_of_scope_findings` of the #18517 round (PR #19107). ⛔ Not folded into that PR — its fence was two test files. ⛔ Ungraded beyond `domain:spec`; grading is triage's.

## The defect

`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` reports a **landed** mutation as **not landed** whenever the replacement string CONTAINS the anchor — which is the shape of *every* 「append `.meta({ title })` / add a flag」 ablation, the most common ablation in this repo.

`validateArgs` refuses `replacement === anchor` but **not** `replacement.includes(anchor)`. The write happens, the blob changes, and the replacement count rises — **three of the tool's four facts hold** — yet the drop check fails by construction and the message reads:

```
the anchor count moved 1 -> 1, a drop of 0
```

⇒ which points the reader at their **edit tooling** rather than at their **anchor**. ⭐ It fails on the SAFE side (no false green; the tree is restored), so this is a **false red plus a misdirecting diagnostic**, ⛔ not a correctness hole.

## Named repro (the reporting dev's, relayed verbatim in substance)

```
node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs \
  --file packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts \
  --anchor "  actionUrl: retiredKey(WIDGET_ACTION_RETIRED('actionUrl'))" \
  --replacement "  actionUrl: retiredKey(WIDGET_ACTION_RETIRED('actionUrl')).meta({ title: 'X' })" \
  --hold
```

⇒ exits 1, measures nothing, restores.

## Why it is worth a card — it cost two seats a round each, independently

- The #18517 dev's **first attempt at all five** ablation legs exited 1 this way and measured nothing; it re-cut the anchor to include the trailing comma and re-ran.
- ⭐ **This seat then hit the same class by hand, in the same hour, on the same file** — a single-line regex that could not reach `aria`'s MULTI-line `retiredKey(` at `:997`, which silently mutated nothing and returned a green run that looked like a pass. ⇒ the failure mode is not one person's slip: an ablation whose mutation did not land is **indistinguishable from a passing control** unless the tool says so clearly, and right now it says something that sends you the wrong way.

## Direction — ⛔ no ruling implied

The fix the dev names is **one up-front refusal beside the byte-identical one**: refuse `replacement.includes(anchor)` with a message that names the append shape and tells the caller to widen the anchor (e.g. to include the trailing comma) — rather than letting the drop check fail later and blame the write.

⚠️ Whoever takes it should also decide whether the drop check is the right invariant at all for an append, or whether the tool should count the **replacement marker** instead. ⛔ This seat does not choose.

## Radius

⚠️ The dev states it plainly: the reading comes from **its own five ablation legs on this one card**, so it is about this one call shape, ⛔ not a survey of the tool. This seat's own hand-rolled repeat of the class is corroboration for the *failure mode*, ⛔ not for the tool's code path (this seat did not run `ablation-replace.mjs` at all — it wrote its own probe and made the same mistake).

⏱️ x; `origin/main` = `2026-09-18T19:57Z` (the stamp was read by the act that wrote this card).

## 查重词

`ablation-replace append mutation` · `replacement contains anchor` · `anchor count drop of 0` · `ablation false red` · `mutation landed reported not landed`

⛔ 本席按章程**不查重**(「立卡者不查重、只附 3–5 查重词」),以上是查重词而不是查重结论。
